chunks: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.
Indeed, the deeds of the children are upon what the child has done, and the deeds of the fathers are upon what the child has done.
And for the Imam, the Proof (peace be upon him).

key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: The Proof (a title for the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between a father's deeds and his child's deeds in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq elaborates on the principle of individual accountability (*mas'uliyya*) by distinguishing between general legal responsibility and specific spiritual attribution, particularly regarding the Ahl al-Bayt. This narration clarifies that while a father's sins do not burden the child, the child's righteous deeds or the father's spiritual legacy can be attributed to the other, emphasizing the unique status of the Imams as the carriers of divine trust and the progeny as the inheritors of their spiritual authority.
